newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall 2.96 pct on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall 2.96 pct on profit-taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares took a battering on Monday, tumbling 2.96 percent as profit-taking wiped out many of last week's gains.
"(Despite last week's gains) there is no real reason for any long-term optimism because there is a lack of domestic money to sustain the rally," one trader said.
The SBI index fell 40.3 points to 1,321.65. In four days of gains last week the blue-chip index rose 3.45 percent.

"There was absolutely no fresh information about a foreign investor comeback and I do not expect any this soon. Prices will stabilize over the next two days," said Predrag Stamenkovic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
In February the central bank blocked international buying, saying foreign investors would have to open special custody accounts in order to trade in Slovenian banks.
Since then the index has dropped over 20 percent, while the average daily volume shrunk to the third of its previous size.
Banks have said the first accounts would be open by the middle of May.
The day's turnover halved to 79.5 million tolars from 159.9 million. Overall 15 shares fell, two rose and 11 were untraded.
Petrol trading company was the most actively traded share, easing 2.28 percent to 18,390 tolars on volume of 1,351 shares and turnover of 24.8 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.21 percent to 6,900 tolars on volume of 52 shares.
Traders said the fall on meagre volume was not significant.
"Dadas is one of the most vulnerable and least interesting shares on our market -- it is interesting only for speculators and no serious investor wants to deal with it," one trader said.
Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska Banka were the top gainer, firming 1.14 percent to 16,000 tolars on volume of 60 shares.
Ordinary shares of trading firm Kovinotehna were the leading decliner among the 11 shares that constitute the blue-chip index, falling 6.04 percent to 451 tolars on volume of 1,314 shares.
Traders said Kovinotehna fell victim to the general profit-taking.
